root_cause.text: During unmount, xfs_unmount_flush_inodes() pushed the AIL while background reclaim and inodegc were still running, allowing concurrent AIL modifications (inodegc dirtying/inserting inodes, reclaim aborting/freeing dirty inodes) that could lead to use-after-free or data corruption.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states: "The unmount sequence in xfs_unmount_flush_inodes() pushed the AIL while background reclaim and inodegc are still running. This is broken independently of any use-after-free issues... Reorder xfs_unmount_flush_inodes() to stop inodegc and cancel background reclaim before pushing the AIL." Patch diff moves `xfs_ail_push_all_sync(mp->m_ail)` after `xfs_inodegc_stop(mp)` and `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&mp->m_reclaim_work)`.

intent_record.what: Updated the comment in xfs_unmount_flush_inodes to explain that inodegc and background reclaim are stopped before pushing the AIL, rather than describing the order as pushing AIL first then reclaiming inodes.
intent_record.how: No functional impact; only the documentation comment was improved to accurately reflect the sequence of operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder operations during unmount to avoid potential races by stopping inodegc and reclaim work before pushing the AIL synchronously.
intent_record.what: Moved the call to xfs_ail_push_all_sync from before xfs_inodegc_stop and cancel_delayed_work_sync to after these calls in the xfs_unmount_flush_inodes function.
intent_record.how: The runtime sequence changes: first inodegc is stopped and reclaim work is canceled, then the AIL is pushed synchronously, followed by reclaim inodes. This ensures that any pending inodegc or reclaim operations are completed before flushing the AIL.
